interest: Tracks 1930s Japanese unemployment insurance proposals and Law No. 42's retirement rules for larger firms, excluding white-collar workers.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
overview: Decimal file 894.5042 covers compulsory, unemployment, and social insurance in Japan between October 1930 and December 1937. The file contains inter-departmental correspondence between the Department of Commerce and the Department of State regarding Japanese unemployment insurance initiatives and life insurance statistics, an instruction sent to the American Consul General in Tokyo urging continued reporting on labor laws, and a detailed despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew confirming that Japanese social legislation (notably Law No. 42 of 1936) did not obligate contributions from foreign nationals employed in U.S. diplomatic and consular missions. In addition, the file includes cross-reference sheets indexing related reports and despatches on Japanese social insurance systems maintained in broader State Department decimal classifications.
